preamble: Translating in Docs doesn't change the document in front of you. It reads it, hands it to a machine translator, and puts the result in a brand new document — yours stays exactly as it was, in its original language. So you're not editing anything here. You're asking Docs to produce a second copy that happens to speak another language.
generalization: The menu bar is sorted by what a command acts on. File is about the document as an object, Format is about how text looks, Insert adds things that weren't there — and Tools is where Docs does work on your behalf: counting, checking, translating. When you can't find a command, ask what kind of thing it is rather than what you want the outcome to be. And note what the copy tells you: anything Docs generates for you tends to arrive as a new document, leaving the original untouched.

steps.intent: Translation isn't something you type, and it isn't a way the text looks — it's a job you hand to Docs to do for you. That kind of thing, where the machine reads your document and gives you something back, lives in one particular menu.
hints: You're not editing, formatting, or adding anything. You're asking Docs to perform a task on the whole document — which menu collects those?
The Tools menu, in the menu bar between Format and Extensions.

wrongHints.Format: A fair guess, because language feels like a property of text. But Format only controls appearance — fonts, spacing, alignment. It can't change what the words say.
wrongHints.Insert: Insert adds something new into this document. Translation doesn't add to this one; it produces a separate one.
wrongHints.File: File deals with the document as an object — naming, copying, exporting. Translation does end up making a copy, but Docs files it under the work being done, not the file being made.
wrongHints.Edit: Edit is for changes you make by hand: undo, cut, paste, find and replace. Translation is work Docs does for you.

steps.intent: Notice the name — Translate document, not translate selection. This command takes the whole thing, every page of it, and there's no way to point it at one paragraph. Clicking it opens a small dialog asking two things: what to call the new copy, and which language it should be in.
hints: You're looking for the one entry that names the whole document as what it acts on.
In the middle of the Tools menu, below Explore and above Voice typing.

wrongHints.Spelling and grammar: Also a machine reading your text and suggesting changes, so the instinct is right. But it corrects the language you already wrote in — it won't move you to another one.
wrongHints.Dictionary: The dictionary defines a word in its own language. Useful for one word, but it won't carry a document across.
wrongHints.Preferences: Preferences is about how Docs behaves as you type — autocorrect, substitutions. It's a setting, not an action performed on this document.
